analysis.summary: Petro Carbon and Chemicals Limited reported its business and financial performance for the year ended May 2025, highlighting stable production volumes and agile operations despite raw material price headwinds. Management discussed strategic expansions, including the commissioning of a 10 MW WHRB power plant, new subsidiary incorporations for backward integration, and approvals for capacity expansion. The company maintains a strong B2B customer base and a high plant capacity utilization rate. Petro Carbon and Chemicals Limited reported a significant increase in financial performance for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with turnover reaching Rs. 57,665.15 lakhs compared to Rs.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that the fortune of the CPC industry is closely linked with the fortune of the aluminium industry.
demand_outlook.quote: Fortune of CPC industry is closely linked with the fortune of aluminium industry

demand_outlook.claim: The calcined petroleum coke industry is expected to grow from USD 3.08 billion in 2025 to USD 4.24 billion by 2034.
demand_outlook.quote: The Calcined Petroleum Coke Market Industry is expected to grow from 3.08 (USD Billion) in 2025 to 4.24 (USD Billion) by 2034.

capex_expansion.claim: Petro Carbon and Chemicals Ltd. received approval from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for an ambitious plant expansion project.
capex_expansion.quote: Petro Carbon and Chemicals Ltd. has received the green light from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, for its ambitious plant expansion project.

capex_expansion.claim: A 10 MW power plant was commissioned at the Haldia factory on March 6, 2025, with a capital expenditure of Rs. 7,111.77 lakhs.
capex_expansion.quote: During the FY 2024-25, 10 Mega Watt Power Plant was commissioned at the Haldia Factory of the Company on 6th March, 2025 and the Company has incurred Capital Expenditure of Rs.7,111.77 lakhs for the same.

capex_expansion.claim: The company received approval from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for a proposed expansion project to install a 72,000 TPA Electrically Calcined Anthracite Plant, 60,000 TPA Coal Tar Distillation Plant, and 48,000 TPA by revamping of Old Carbon Paste Plant.
capex_expansion.quote: The Company has got approval of Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, vide their letter dated 23rd April, 2025, for proposed expansion project of the existing plant located in Haldia, West Bengal by installation of 72,000 TPA Electrically Calcined Anthracite Plant, 60,000 TPA Coal Tar Distillation Plant and 48,000 TPA by revamping of Old Carbon Paste Plant.

margins_costs.claim: Management stated that the CPC industry faced headwinds in FY 2025 primarily due to elevated raw material prices, which could not be fully passed on to customers resulting in margin compression.
margins_costs.quote: The CPC industry faced headwinds in FY 2025, primarily due to elevated raw material prices. These increases could not be fully passed on to customers, resulting in margin compression and a weakened bottom line across the sector.

orders_capacity.claim: The plant has an installed capacity of approximately 93,744 tons per annum of CPC.
orders_capacity.quote: The Plant has a capacity of approximately 93,744 tons per annum of CPC and the plant comprises an area of around 30 acres with good infrastructure facilities like own railway sliding inside the plant premises itself facilitating unloading / loading of wagons, along with yard / shed to store both Raw Petroleum Coke (RPC) / Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC).

orders_capacity.claim: Production of Calcined Petroleum Coke for fiscal year 2024-25 was 84,305.500 MT against 91,541.200 MT in financial year 2023-24.
orders_capacity.quote: Production of CPC for fiscal year 2024-25 was 84,305.500 MT against 91,541.200 MT in financial year 2023-24.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board of Directors decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year under review in order to conserve resources for future expansion and working capital requirements.
capital_allocation.quote: In order to conserve resources for future expansion and working capital requirements, your Directors have decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year under review.

capital_allocation.claim: During the financial year ended 31st March, 2025, the company spent Rs. 87.77 Lakhs on corporate social responsibility activities against a required amount of Rs. 86.88 Lakhs.
capital_allocation.quote: In terms of Section 135(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 read with the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014, the Company was required to spend an amount of Rs.86.88 Lakhs. During the financial year ended 31st March, 2025, the Company has spent Rs.87.77 Lakhs.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company reported heavy reliance on imports, especially low-sulphur RPC from the U.S. and other Europe and Asian countries, affecting cost and availability.
risks_headwinds.quote: Heavy reliance on imports (esp. low-sulphur RPC from the U.S. and Other Europe and Asian countries) affects cost and availability.

risks_headwinds.claim: The energy-intensive calcination process raises operational costs, especially during power and fuel inflation.
risks_headwinds.quote: Energy-intensive calcination process raises operational costs, especially during power/fuel inflation.

risks_headwinds.claim: Demand is tied to aluminium, steel, and battery sectors, each sensitive to economic cycles.
risks_headwinds.quote: Demand tied to aluminium, steel, and battery sectors—each sensitive to economic cycles.

risks_headwinds.claim: Trade restrictions and anti-dumping duties or export/import restrictions in key markets impact pricing.
risks_headwinds.quote: Anti-dumping duties or export/import restrictions in key markets (e.g., China, USA and West Asia Market) impact pricing.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company imports more than 90% of its raw materials from foreign suppliers and faces foreign exchange risk.
risks_headwinds.quote: The company imports more than 90% of its raw materials from foreign suppliers as a result of which the company faces foreign exchange risk.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company adopted a forex policy in June 2023 ensuring 100% hedging, where initial 50% of exposure is hedged immediately on LC opening and remaining 50% upon obtaining SBLC due date.
risks_headwinds.quote: In order to minimize this risk, the company adopted a forex policy in June, 2023 which ensured 100% hedging. As per hedging policy, initial 50% of the exposure is hedged immediately on LC opening & remaining 50% hedging is done on obtaining SBLC due date.

risks_headwinds.claim: The supply of raw petroleum coke in India is limited and the company is dependent on imports for more than 90% of its raw material.
risks_headwinds.quote: In India the supply of RPC is limited. Most of the supplies in India are from four plants of IOCL which is purchased by various MSMEs operating in vicinity of IOCL plants. The company, is therefore, dependent on imports and has to import more than 90% of its raw material from foreign suppliers.

management_commitments.claim: Indian exports are expected to reach US$ 1 trillion by 2030.
management_commitments.quote: According to Minister of Commerce and Industry, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and Textiles Mr. Piyush Goyal, Indian exports are expected to reach US$ 1 trillion by 2030.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
